_about: Researched profile (web sources listed), compiled 2026-11-07. Shipped with Headroom.
name: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D

profile.arch: Zen 5 (Granite Ridge), 8C/16T, 96 MB L3 (2nd-gen 3D V-Cache, under the cores: full multiplier/PBO unlocked, unlike 7800X3D)
profile.tuning_method: PBO + per-core Curve Optimizer (negative) + Max Boost Clock Override. Set in BIOS; Headroom finds the CO values at runtime with CoreCycler (PawnIO), which are temporary until entered in BIOS.

community_results.settings: PBO limits removed, +200 MHz, scalar 10x, CO -10 all-core
community_results.result: +200 MHz boost ceiling, stable; small app gains
CB R23 22,689 MT / 2,054 ST, 5.2 GHz all-core
CB R23 22,837-23,517 MT / 2,142-2,144 ST; +200 was not stable at light all-core loads for that chip, +125 used
CB R23 23,006 MT / 2,154 ST at 5,425 MHz, ~144 W package
LOWER power than stock thanks to CO; gain is mostly efficiency
big chip-to-chip variation; Cyberpunk 1440p ~+1 fps; can hurt 1% lows if unstable

notes: Do NOT raise PPT/TDC/EDC: on an X3D part the gain is ~0 and it only adds heat.
Keep VSOC at or below 1.20 V (EXPO can push it to 1.25-1.30 V). The 2025 '9800X3D burned socket' reports were mostly ASRock boards with high SoC power; keep the ASUS BIOS updated.
Platform Thermal Throttle Limit = 85 C is a hardware-level ceiling: the CPU itself clocks down before it can cook, whatever any software does.
Ryzen 9000 often FREEZES instead of rebooting on a bad CO value: press reset; CoreCycler resumes and raises that core by 1.
